title: RAW UNREVIEWED: three thunder sounds retain separate material causes
summary: In the already owned complete Megenberg II.25, three reported thunder sounds are explained by three different vapour/cloud configurations: a surrounding cloud breaking at one side, a lengthwise rupture of cloud and air, and piecewise vapour emerging in succession. A whole-content reading would have to keep each sound attached to its stated cause and preserve the serial character of the third case. This is a source-only exploratory proposal, not a Voynich identification or a tested meaning.

design.mechanism: Three sound descriptions each bind to a distinct cause in one continuous thunder account; the third cause additionally binds successive pieces to repeated crackling.
design.unit: Megenberg, Buch der Natur II.25, owned complete text at research_registry/proposals/laufenberg_f85r2_20260926/external_cache/megenberg_II25_complete_20260927.txt, page 92 lines 30-36 through page 93 lines 1-7; retain the full chapter as the eventual source unit.
design.contrast: Enclosed vapour breaking cloud on one side versus a lengthwise tear through cloud and air versus successive piecewise vapour release. Their sound analogies are respectively an air-filled bladder, a lengthwise torn cloth, and wood or nuts crackling in fire.
design.prediction: A proposed complete source-to-target account must distinguish the three cause-to-sound pairings without swapping their causes, treating all as one generic thunder noise, or turning illustrative analogies into extra observed events. It must retain the preceding common vapour account and the following lightning effects and objections.
design.source_status: Already owned primary transcription; no new source, image, target passage or reserve opened for this proposal.
predecessors: IDEA000588 keeps one event across earlier sight and later hearing; it does not propose the three causal sound subclasses.
IDEA000595 distinguishes deficient and excessive heat at different seasonal thunder stages; it does not bind the three reported sound qualities to three stated local causes.
IDEA000597 tests a co-falling stone identity claim by injury; it does not own the three acoustic explanations.
IDEA000601 addresses selective lightning injury, not thunder sound production.
design.assumptions_and_limits: The source asserts historical natural-philosophical explanations, not verified modern physics. The account does not imply that all three sounds occur in one storm, that sound form identifies a unique actual cloud event, or that any Voynich form names thunder. Separate complete clauses remain a viable rival to a reusable construction. Zero target referents or lexemes are independently bound.
design.smallest_future_test: Only if an independently justified target-side thunder or acoustic passage and a full reading become available: freeze the three source pairings and ask whether one written rule covers all three while also accounting for the full admitted target unit and known counterexamples. Stop as missing binding if the independent target link is absent.
design.future_budget: At most 30 minutes including predecessor and primary review, proposal freeze, bounded comparison and publication; no decoder or new corpus work is justified by this raw card.
design.duplicate_screen: Bounded ideas search/duplicates and route-check on thunder sound, enclosure, tear and piecewise vapour returned IDEA000595, IDEA000588 and older source history but no identical declared design. Lexical navigation does not certify novelty or scientific eligibility.
